title: Latency-tail instrumentation and hybrid golden synthesis for bench harness
creator: Priya Sharma
description: Goal: Extend our benchmark harness to more reliably detect regressions that impact tail latency and prefill/decoder scheduling trade-offs across kernel-routing variants. Scope: (1) instrument and surface heavy-tail quantiles (p95/p99/p999) per-kernel and per-stage (prefill vs decode); (2) introduce a hybrid golden synthesis flow that composes deterministic golden baselines from micro-cohorts instead of single monolithic seeds; (3) add CI perf gates which run lightweight sampled synths on PRs and full guard runs nightly. Success metrics: Canary CI should catch >90% of synthetic tail-shift regressions introduced in runtime, reduce undetected prefill-prefill-to-decode regressions in canary by 75%, and keep PR feedback time for the lightweight gate under 30 minutes. Motivation: Existing golden baselines are brittle to workload composition shifts and under-emphasize kernel routing locality and attention optimization interactions. Several incidents (see ENG-210001) showed regressions that only manifested in the 99.9th percentile under mixed prefill/decode loads. This ticket implements harness-level changes (workload templating, micro-cohort seeding, sentinel quantiles) plus CI integration and documentation for on-call triage and follow-ups.
comments: [2025-11-05] Priya Sharma: Kickoff sync. Agreed tech approach: create micro-cohort sampler (length/temperature/model-variant axes) and produce a composite golden by stitching per-cohort golden seeds. This reduces variance from monolithic corpus changes.

[2025-11-06] Ethan Cole: PoC for per-kernel quantile instrumentation added under runtime/telemetry. Collectors emit per-request tags: kernel_variant, scheduling_path (prefill|decode), seq_len_bucket. Early tests show p99 upward drift under hybrid prefills when kernel selection falls back to 'fallback-quant' for short sequences.

[2025-11-10] Design review (Anya M.): Suggested UX for console: surface a heatmap over kernel_variant x scheduling_path for p95/p99 so oncall can quickly spot which kernel causes tail shifts. Will file a follow-up in product-management if we want polished UX.

[2025-11-12] QA (Jordan Li): Added stress harness that replays stochastic traces with seeded RNG and validates deterministic golden outputs for baseline kernels. Found nondeterministic KV-cache misses in run#23; created ENG-47245 as a blocker dependency.

[2025-11-14] Ethan Cole: Implemented hybrid golden synthesis pipeline (stitcher) in bench-orch. It accepts micro-cohort manifests and outputs a lockfile with reference token-level latencies and checksum. Added mapping: cohort -> canonical seed id.

[2025-11-15] Priya Sharma: Decision: CI will have two gates: (A) lightweight PR gate that runs 10 sampled micro-cohorts (~20min wall) against a diff runner to detect large regressions in p95/p99; (B) nightly full guard with the complete composite golden including p999 checking. Rationale: balance fast feedback and thorough nightly coverage.

[2025-11-16] Ethan Cole: Open PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8123 implements metric exporters for per-kernel p50/p95/p99/p999 and a bench harness adapter. Also added a configurable alert threshold mapping (relative% vs absolute ms).

[2025-11-17] Priya Sharma: Security note: no model payloads are persisted outside encrypted artifact storage. Bench lockfiles are treated as sensitive for internal tracing but do not contain customer text. security_review_required set to false per initial Sec review (ticket SEC-1421 covers KMS policies).

[2025-11-18] QA (Jordan Li): Lightweight CI gate run on the PR caught a 12% p99 increase for kernel_variant 'quant8-fast' when decode scheduling was set to batch-size=8. Adding regression guard to map decode batch size to recommended kernel or block change with blocker severity.

[2025-11-18] Ethan Cole: Next steps: (1) finish PR feedback and merge runtime exporters; (2) wire the PR gate into CI and tune thresholds (initial mapping: p95 +10% or p99 +15% triggers failure); (3) add runbook snippet for investigating kernel-induced tail shifts; (4) schedule a cross-team demo with Platform and Console on 2025-11-25.
